speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information given that online advertisements on social media platforms are easily uploaded by individuals based on the social media platforms' rules of engagement, what are the safeguards that the Ministry has put in place to ensure that these rules of engagement are relevant and in line with local regulations and best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Marketers are also expected to familiarise themselves with the relevant laws and guidelines on each social media service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This includes putting in place specific measures to protect children, such as ensuring that children do not receive targeted advertisements detrimental to their physical or mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It has been observed that the process is much easier for individuals and companies to put up their advertisements on social media platforms, given that many of such platforms encourage boosting or ad buying proactively to their users.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is unclear what these social media platforms do to verify the content of these ads.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In a recent case, a water purification company made certain arguably uninformed claims about the safety of Singapore tap water.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Public Utilities Board has since issued advisories for that.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There has been other cases of companies who have also done similar things.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Are there regular proactive dialogues the Ministry of Communications and Information holds with these popular social media platforms on their ad rules and what more can be done to advise companies and individuals on responsible advertising claims?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we work on a local advisory notice embedded on social media platforms before and ad is triggered?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As I mentioned earlier my main reply, commercial advertising in Singapore, like the one that Ms Yeo had referred to, is regulated by the ASAS and the ASAS is established under the Consumer Association of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: At the heart of matter that Ms Yeo had raised is whether the advertisement meets the threshold or stipulation that is legal, decent, honest and truthful, and whether the parties like the marketeers, the advertisers and the media involved in displaying, presenting or putting in place the advertisements, meet the standards of ethical behaviour, ethical conduct.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are all the guidelines stimulated by the advertising council.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, what is the recourse if somebody believes that an advertisement breaches some of these stipulations or code of ethical conduct?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: When ASAS receives the complaint, it will first advise the advertiser to amend the advertisement.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There are direct financial costs to such amendments.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Recalcitrant companies could be referred to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore, or CCCS, for investigation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And errant companies may be issued injunction orders by the Court.
